clue.text: Present for plucky player in Cardiff ?

definitions.text: Present for plucky player in Cardiff ?

parts.words: Present for plucky player in Cardiff
parts.note: a gift for someone who plucks strings, living in the capital of Wales, would be that nation's own stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Choosing a gift for a guitarist who lives in the Welsh capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' looks like 'brave' but means 'who plucks strings'; Cardiff points to Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The triple-strung harp is the traditional instrument of Wales, plucked by its player.

clue.text: Irish port a cheap drink once?

definitions.meaning: a harbour city in south-east Ireland, famed for its crystal glass
read as ..., a drink costing a penny, d being the pre-1971 British penny

explanation.walkthrough: Before decimal currency in 1971, d stood for the British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour city in south-east Ireland, and, split up, a drink sold for one old penny.

clue.text: IRA members get in £500 from Scottish gentleman

indicators.note: get in says the rearranged letters go inside the money

parts.note: £ is L (libra, the pound) and 500 is D in Roman numerals

indicators.note: members suggests the letters of the IRA split up and reordered

explanation.surface: Republican paramilitaries extort five hundred pounds from a Scottish landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound sign is L, from Latin libra, and Roman D is 500; 'members' looks like people in the organisation but tells you to reorder its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor, the local gentleman with an estate.

clue.text: Greeting we'd reverenced

parts.note: hallo is a greeting, a variant of hello
the letters of we'd as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A greeting that we would have treated with reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held sacred and venerated has been treated with reverence.

clue.text: Last drink the' Borgias' guest might ask for ?

definitions.text: Last drink the' Borgias' guest might ask for ?

parts.words: Last drink the' Borgias' guest might ask for
parts.note: the Borgia family were notorious poisoners, so their dinner guest would want a cure for the drink

explanation.surface: A dinner guest of the infamous Borgias orders one final glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last drink' suggests a nightcap; for a Borgia guest the last drink would be the remedy against poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy counteracting poison is exactly what a guest of notorious poisoners would need.

clue.text: District ARP organizer and his group

indicators.note: organizer suggests putting the letters of ARP into a new order
group as a verb means arrange, so the letters of his are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wartime air-raid warden organizes his local team.
explanation.walkthrough: ARP was Air Raid Precautions in wartime Britain; 'organizer' reorders it to PAR and 'group' reorders his to ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a local area served by a church, a small administrative district.

clue.text: Possibly a sect of importance in India

definitions.text: Possibly a sect of importance in India

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words a sect may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A remark that some religious group carries weight on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a rearranged 'a sect' gives a social grouping that matters greatly in Indian society.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary social class has long been a powerful structure in Indian society, a sort of sect in the loose sense.

clue.text: Snappy addition to tripper's outfit?

parts.note: snappy means taking snapshots, the gadget a day-tripper hangs round the neck

explanation.surface: Adding a smart accessory to the holidaymaker's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappy' suggests stylish clothing; it means a device that takes snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for taking snapshots is a standard part of a tourist's kit.

clue.text: Dash out to the one continental quarter supplying teacake

parts.note: to sally is to rush out, as in a sortie
in French l'un means the one
N, north, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone rushes out to a French district to buy a teacake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' makes 'the one' French: L'UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sally Lunn is a large light sweet bun from Bath, served at tea.

clue.text: It is the very of the moon " (othello)

definitions.text: It is the very of the moon " (othello)

parts.words: It is the very of the moon " (othello)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Othello Act V: 'It is the very — of the moon; she comes more nearer earth than she was wont'

explanation.surface: A gap in a line spoken by Othello to be filled.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello blames the moon straying too near the earth for driving men mad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello the word means a wandering off course, the moon's straying from its path.

clue.text: One of three scored ?

parts.note: reads as one sibling from a multiple birth, but scored means written in a musical score, where three notes are played in the time of two

explanation.surface: Someone's third child scores a goal, or one of three players got on the scoresheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of three' suggests a sibling of a multiple birth; 'scored' shifts it to music, a group of three notes in the time of two.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a child born in a set of three and a musical group of three notes share the name.

clue.text: Rose Walker

definitions.meaning: a climbing rose variety with long trailing stems
someone who hikes for pleasure in the countryside

explanation.definitionFit: A climbing rose with long trailing stems, and a person who hikes over the countryside for pleasure.

clue.text: Jockey wasn't up for the Wild West show

parts.note: a jockey rode, i.e. was riding, in a race
in racing a jockey who is 'up' is riding; not up gives a nought, O, for no mount

explanation.surface: A jockey stood down from a race, so went to see a cowboy display instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is racing slang for being the rider of a horse; the charade puts RODE beside O, nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a cowboy spectacle of riding and roping that grew out of the American frontier.

clue.text: Warship named Siva ?

definitions.meaning: a fast naval vessel armed against submarines and torpedo boats
in Hindu belief Siva is the god of destruction, one of the trinity with Brahma and Vishnu

explanation.definitionFit: A fast naval escort vessel, and the title of the Hindu god Siva, the force of destruction in the trinity.

clue.text: Work before race and a light entertainment

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
ere is an old word for before
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone works before a race and then relaxes with some light entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, light musical stage piece with spoken dialogue is a lighter form of opera.

clue.text: Sporting extension unpopular in Dartmoor

definitions.meaning: additional minutes played when a match is level at full time
Dartmoor is a prison, where a longer sentence would not be welcome

explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a well-known high-security prison in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra minutes added to a drawn match, and a longer spell inside that no convict would welcome.

clue.text: Pull round the point for a breather

indicators.note: round says the word for pull goes around the compass point

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Hauling something round a headland, then stopping for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' looks like a rest; it is an organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing organ is literally something that breathes.

clue.text: Garage trouble-shooter ?

parts.note: a trouble-shooter fixes problems, but this workshop tool literally shoots lubricant at squeaky trouble spots

explanation.surface: A mechanic who sorts out problems at the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble-shooter' suggests a person; it is a tool that shoots grease.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand pump that forces lubricant into car joints is a staple tool in a workshop.

clue.text: Pole has done trip on foot, perhaps

definitions.note: a phrase standing for something worn on the foot, a noun

parts.note: S, south, is one of the poles

indicators.note: trip suggests the words has done stumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A Polish man has made a journey on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality; it is the south pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas beach shoe is worn on the foot, perhaps on the sand.

clue.text: This pace to break records ?

parts.note: a very fast speed that might set new records, also the act of breaking gramophone records

explanation.surface: Someone running at a speed fast enough to set a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: A very fast pace and the act of splitting vinyl discs share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for very fast, as a pace, and literally splitting gramophone discs.

clue.text: Many consumed in time

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A lot of food was eaten during a set period.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use 'many' for a large Roman numeral such as D.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a specific point in the calendar, a particular time.

clue.text: Writer in the crew Lane collected

indicators.note: collected suggests the words crew and Lane gathered together and rearranged

explanation.surface: An author is found among the crew that someone called Lane gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: D H Lawrence or T E Lawrence: either is a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: D H Lawrence was an English novelist and poet, a famous writer.

clue.text: Agreeing to give a rise, say

definitions.note: a gerund, the act of agreeing, a noun

indicators.note: say signals that a word sounding the same is meant

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to give a worker a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a rise' suggests a pay rise; it is a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement or consent.

clue.text: Resin-it's a variety used in decoration

indicators.note: used in says the rearranged letters are placed within the decoration

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a medal or decoration

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form of the letters of it's a

explanation.surface: A resin of some kind used for ornamental work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoration' here means a military medal, not ornament; 'variety' tells you to reorder the letters of it's a, and 'used in' places them inside the medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a gum exuded from the lentisk tree, a natural resin.

clue.text: Prom musicians I do like to hear:

definitions.text: Prom musicians I do like to hear:

parts.words: Prom musicians I do like to hear
parts.note: Prom is the seaside promenade, and the music-hall song 'I do like to be beside the seaside' mentions these players

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying the musicians at a concert Prom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests the London concert season, but here it is a seaside promenade; the old song 'I do like to be beside the seaside' goes on to its bandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of trumpets, cornets and tubas traditionally played on bandstands along seaside promenades.

clue.text: No end of dairy produce in Montana

definitions.note: the phrase stands for a landform found in Montana, a noun

indicators.note: no end of says the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: butter is a dairy product

explanation.surface: Montana has plenty of milk and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of'; it removes the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep isolated flat-topped hill, typical of Montana and the American West.

clue.text: Church leader chooses certain Christians

indicators.note: the leader of the word church is its opening letter

parts.note: opts means chooses

explanation.surface: A bishop picks particular believers for a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' looks like a bishop; it is just the first letter of church.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the ancient Egyptian church are a distinct community of Christians.

clue.text: Legendary king one taking baby's place

indicators.note: taking means the baby's carriage takes in the numeral

parts.note: a pram is the place where a baby lies
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old king climbs into the infant's spot.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into PRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Associated with Britannia aircraft?

definitions.meaning: the figure of Britannia on coins holds a three-pronged spear
the Hawker Siddeley airliner of that name, a British jet

explanation.definitionFit: Britannia is pictured holding a three-pronged spear, and a British jet airliner of the 1960s bore its name.

clue.text: Could be greeting in Southend? Not very well

indicators.note: Southend-on-Sea in Essex has an accent that drops its H, so a word starting with H is said without it

parts.note: ailing means not very well, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone waving at a friend on the Essex coast while feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is an Essex seaside town whose local accent drops initial H, so 'calling out to' and 'poorly' are said the same there.
explanation.definitionFit: Hailing someone is calling out a greeting to them.

clue.text: Note opening item in sports programme

parts.note: E is a musical note
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A remark about the first item on the bill at a sports meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening item' reads as one phrase; split it, 'opening' giving VENT and 'item in sports programme' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Each separate race or contest on a sports card is called by this name.

clue.text: My clanger embarrassed the priest

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests the words my clanger thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's blunder in front of the vicar left the vicar red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister of the church.
